- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.1) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 1–2 days), leading to overshoot; cap forecast peak at 1.5x recent high or 1.2x prior peak.
- In 30-day horizon, model underestimates mean-reversion zones — if price has drifted >1.5σ from 18-day mean, forecast should revert toward mean.
- If sentiment history shows rising optimism (e.g., 0.27→0.53→0.53), model often fails to anticipate further rise; add 0.1–0.3 to forecast for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is flat or negative for 3+ days, model tends to ignore downward momentum; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0 if price has been declining.
- Model often lags sentiment shifts — if sentiment rises sharply, delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days; if sentiment drops, adjust 1–2 days early.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows >10% deviation from 18-day moving average, model is biased — apply mean-reversion correction with 0.8–0.9 multiplier to recent trend.
